topic: Jess's landlord has finally put a smart meter in her damp flat, and the app shows her electricity minute by minute. She has just told the table she can see the exact minute Matt gets up in the night to make toast, and that she's started checking it at work.

plan.hint: someone who half-knows something surprising about electricity, the grid or what meters reveal first says plainly they can't swear to it, then says it at full strength
before pushing back, someone offers back an accurate version of what another person just claimed, in their own words, as a check; that person confirms it next turn
someone pushes back with a counterexample; the person under pressure welcomes it and folds it in as making their own point stronger
someone remarks on the table itself as play (everyone suddenly checking their own phones, everyone confessing at once, how fast they've all turned on Matt) and uses it as a move

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Hang on, at work? You're checking your boyfriend's toast at work?

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Every lunch. Two forty-three, toast.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Every— every night?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: How d'you know it's toast, though? Could be the kettle, kettle's a much bigger spike than a toaster.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: I can't— don't hold me to this, but somebody worked out which film people were watching. From the meter. Off the telly alone.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: No, the kettle's this big fat wall, that's me at seven. Two forty-three's a little bump, nothing for four minutes, then another little bump. He goes back for a second round.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Mind the— no, got it. So you know about the second round, and nothing about why he's up

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Hungry, I should think.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Same minute every night, though? That's not hunger, Hugh, that's— nobody's hungry to the minute, that's something waking him.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: What's your heating— is something on a timer in that flat? Old storage heaters clunk on at— no, hang on, that'd be on your app anyway.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: I haven't asked him. Can't, can I?
T.full: I haven't asked him. Can't, can I? Then he knows I've been sat in the staffroom watching his toast.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Unless he— unless he knows already.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Wait, so you're— you're saying he knows she's got the app open, and the two forty-three is for her? Like he's doing the toast to be seen doing the toast?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Yes, that. A little show at two forty-three. Matt's not daft, he knows she's watching, so it's a message. Thinking of you, here's toast.

T.event: Jess's phone buzzes face-down against her glass
T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Oh God, is that
T.full: Oh God, is that— no. Mum.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Don't knock it, I've got Cai's little dot on my phone, I watched it sit outside a girl's house for forty minutes Tuesday.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Forty min— did you text him?

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: No. Well— I typed one.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: I know the minute Will comes in off the lane at night, the dogs go quiet for him and for nobody else. Never let on
T.full: I know the minute Will comes in off the lane at night, the dogs go quiet for him and for nobody else. Never let on. He thinks I sleep like a stone.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: No, that's for me, that is. Will knows. Nobody gets the dogs that quiet unless he knows who's lying awake listening.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: I'm not lying awake. I'm reading.

T.event: Jess's phone buzzes again and she flips it over
T.speaker: Jess
T.line: It's— no. No, it's the landlord.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Whose name's the account in? Cos if he pays the bill, he's got the same app, he's had your toast
T.full: Whose name's the account in? Cos if he pays the bill, he's got the same app, he's had your toast since— since whenever.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: It's in— it's in mine. I think it's mine? Oh God, he texted me at half two last week. About the damp.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Half two. So the landlord's up as well. Matt, you, Rhi's Cai, Hugh's dogs, half the town awake waiting for toast.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Which night? Which— what night was that?

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Tuesday, I think, or— hang on, why's everyone— Femi's got his work face on, you're all building a timeline on my boyfriend.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Guilty. But a phone on charge barely shows up, so anyone lying awake texting at half two
T.full: Guilty. But a phone on charge barely shows up, so anyone lying awake texting at half two, your app never sees them.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Like you, Jess. At half two.

T.event: the back room door bangs open and a cold draught comes through
T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Shut that, it's freezing— I was up because— no, the toaster wakes me. It pops. I'm lying there listening for the pop.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Lambing does that. You lie there listening for the one noise and you're awake— you're awake before it's even come.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Before the— so who wakes
T.full: Before the— so who wakes first?

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: No, it's both— it's both of them. You wake before your alarm, most people do, the body's half— half counting. She's up for the toast before Matt's
T.full: No, it's both— it's both of them. You wake before your alarm, most people do, the body's half— half counting. She's up for the toast before Matt's even—

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Oh no. Am I waking him?

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Do you put a lamp on?

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: No, I just lie there in the— in the dark, I don't even turn over, I'm sort of holding my breath for the—

judgements.speaker: Femi
judgements.reason: In a five-person exchange, Femi first lowers his own authority ('I can't— don't hold me to this'), then states the meter-reveals-the-film claim as flat, emphatic fact ('Off the telly alone'), so the flag is what licenses the full-strength claim rather than a withholding.

judgements.speaker: Femi
judgements.reason: In a talk involving at least five people, Femi offers back a candidate version of Danny's half-finished point in turn 12 ('you're saying he knows she's got the app open...'), and Danny confirms it in turn 14 ('Yes, that'), though Femi does not go on to disagree as the group reading's typical framing suggests.

judgements.speaker: Danny
judgements.reason: Hugh's 'never let on' example implies Will doesn't know he's being watched, which cuts against Danny's frame, and Danny welcomes it ('that's for me, that is') and turns it into further proof that the watched one knows, extending his claim from Matt to Will in a multi-party stretch (Femi, Rhi, Sunny, Hugh, Jess all active).

judgements.speaker: Jess
judgements.reason: In a five-person stretch, Jess calls out how the table is talking ("you're all building a timeline on my boyfriend"), and the table takes it up: Femi owns it with "Guilty" and keeps building, and Sunny turns the timeline back onto Jess.
